members.note: One clamp-assign-push-broadcast road, so the property, the field and the event can never disagree about the number.
FDreamSpinBoxStyle: the two step faces' colour set, the field's, plus sizes. Same role as FSpinBoxStyle, different shape.
The setter re-spells the number already showing: a digit count nobody applied is not a format.
Turning it on re-snaps the value the control is holding, not only the next one.
Turning it off during a scrub ends that scrub and commits, rather than leaving a gesture nothing will finish.
The library's existing spelling, kept because .dui authors it. GetDelta/SetDelta carry the UMG name and forward to the same field.
Setter clamps away from zero, the same floor the scrub arithmetic applies.

A font DATA ASSET, not an FSlateFontInfo: the size is Style.FontSize and the outline belongs to the text style. GetFont/SetFont read and write it. The two step glyphs take the same one -- a minus sign in a different typeface from the number beside it is the one thing a shared style must not produce. Null leaves the paragraph on the font it has.
EDreamUITextParagraphHorizontalAlign, the library's one paragraph-alignment enum. Default Center, which is where the built-in tree has always put the number.
A floor under the control's own width and under what the value's paragraph asks a content-sized parent for. 0 = no opinion.
Pushed to the typed-entry field's UUITextInput. Defaults to Number, which is the keyboard that field already derived from its DecimalNumber input type -- the same keyboard, said outright.
Pushed to the field's behaviour; default TextCommitOnDismiss, which is what it did.
b-prefixed. Default false, the same as UMG's.
Default TRUE where UMG's is false: a spin box is filled in one entry after another, and this is what it has always done.
Appearance lives in the style struct; the value text and the two step glyphs share it.
Fires on every value a scrub passes through.
Same moment; carries the value alone, without UMG's ETextCommit -- see EditableTextBox.json for why that enum is not spoken here.
Carries the value the scrub started from, where UMG's carries nothing. Fires when the drag is recognised, and the travel before that moves no value, as in SSpinBox.
Forwards to StepSize.
Forwards to SetStepSize, which re-snaps the held value while delta snapping is on.
Returns float's floor when the bound is switched off, exactly as UMG's does, because that is what every caller then clamps with.
States the bound AND clamps the held value into it, so a range that moved under a value cannot leave it outside.
bOverride_MinValue defaults to TRUE, unlike UMG's: every spin box that exists is clamped into 0..100 and an unbounded default would change all of them.
The stated scrub bottom, or float's floor when there is none. GetSliderMinValue is the EFFECTIVE one, which falls back to the value range.
The scrub falls back to the value range, which is what it did before there were slider bounds at all.
Moves through SetStyle or the project sheet; a second setter writing the inline struct would be silently inert whenever StyleSource is the sheet.
With bOverride_MinValue beside it, the same pair UMG uses. Default ticked, because every existing spin box is bounded.
Unticked by default: the scrub sweeps the value range unless someone narrows it.
